strategy.observation: GitLab has 2,500+ team members and 5,500+ contributors, and it says its workforce is all-remote and spread around the world.
strategy.offer_link: For a documentation org supporting a distributed company of that scale, contract technical writers could add bandwidth for release notes and migration guides when coordination and turnaround matter most.
hypotheses: The documentation team may be absorbing a steady stream of release-related writing work.
A distributed contributor base may create coordination overhead for keeping docs consistent.
They may have occasional spikes where temporary writing support would help clear backlog faster.
strategy.angle: With 2,500+ team members and 5,500+ contributors spread around the world, release notes and migration guides may be a coordination-heavy load for your docs team.
strategy.fit_reason: Contract technical writers are a plausible fit for an engineering documentation function at a large, globally distributed software company, especially for recurring release notes and migration guides that can benefit from extra writing capacity.

draft.subject: Docs support for GitLab
draft.body:
With 2,500+ team members and 5,500+ contributors spread around the world, release notes and migration guides can turn into a lot of coordination.

I contract technical writers to cover that kind of work when docs teams need extra bandwidth. It helps keep release writing moving without pulling your core team into every draft and revision.

Do you ever bring in contract writers for release notes or migration guides when the workload spikes?
